prompt: A pizza has radius $6$ inches. One slice has a central angle of $\frac{\pi}{3}$ radians. What is the area of that slice?
hint: Sector area is $A = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$ — note the square and the one-half.

hints.text: Sector area is $A = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$ — note the square and the one-half.

explanation: The area of a sector with the angle in radians is $A = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$.
That gives $18 \times \frac{\pi}{3} = 6\pi$ square inches, about 18.8 square inches.

alternativeExplanations.title: Fraction of the whole pizza
steps: $\frac{\pi}{3}$ radians is $60^\circ$, which is $\frac{1}{6}$ of the pizza.
The whole pizza has area $\pi r^2 = 36\pi$.
One sixth of $36\pi$ is $6\pi$ square inches — the same answer.
